episodes.214127: Intense daytime heating combined with near record monsoon moisture under an upper level high centered over west-central NM July 24th, resulting in scattered to numerous thunderstorms across the higher terrain, Rio Grande Valley, and eastern plains during the afternoon and evening hours. Thunderstorms produced debris flows on and downstream of the South Fork burn scar in Ruidoso, flash flooding and thunderstorm wind damage due to wind gusts up to 78 mph in Albuquerque, and flash flooding in the Zuni Pueblo. Thunderstorms tapered off after sunset and during the overnight hours due to the loss of daytime heating. The storm activity on July 24th helped develop a disturbance over the state going into July 25th resulting in another round of thunderstorm development across western and central NM during the afternoon hours. Thunderstorms produced more flash flooding in Zuni Pueblo and a debris flow at Perk Canyon in Ruidoso. Thunderstorms developed over the higher terrain once again during the afternoon hours on July 26th with one thunderstorm producing a 61 mph gust at Sierra Blanca Regional Airport.
episodes.214184: Training thunderstorms developed across southwest Middle Tennessee during the early morning of July 25, 2026. Precipitable water amounts exceeding 2 inches allowed these thunderstorms to produce very heavy rainfall, and repeated rounds of this caused flash flooding across portions of Wayne County. Radar estimates and gauges in the area reported 3 to 4 inches of rain during this event which caused some roadways to become impassable.
episodes.214261: Two individuals were struck by lightning near the north end of Wrightsville Beach, NC.
episodes.214311: During the late afternoon of July 24, slow-moving thunderstorms led to localized flooding issues in the Rainbow City, Southside, Wellington, Leesburg, and Pratt City areas. The next afternoon, a decaying mesoscale convective system (MCS) moved through Walker and Jefferson counties, causing minor instances of tree damage.
episodes.214317: Strong thunderstorms moved through central Montana, some of which became severe.
episodes.214421: Cluster of thunderstorms, fueled by MLCAPE values in excess of 1000 J/KG, developed along the Mogollon Rim during the early afternoon hours on the 25th. The activity gradually moved west to southwestward with time affecting portions of Gila County, with a severe thunderstorm near Roosevelt Estates sending strong outflow winds into the Globe area and causing a downed tree and power line. Eventually, a well-organized outflow boundary emanating from the thunderstorm complex developed and moved southwestward into the lower deserts of south-central AZ. With DCAPE values of at least 1500 J/KG, strong winds from the outflow was a major threat with widespread 35-55 mph gusts observed across much of the south-central lower deserts, with additional showers and embedded lightning developing along the outflow, although activity was sub-severe. Some minor wind impacts were observed as these strong outflow winds materialized, including several boats capsizing at Lake Pleasant and downed power lines near Florence. Areas of blowing dust were also observed across portions of Pinal County, although visibilities for the most part remained above one mile.
episodes.215160: A cool front slowly shifted southward through Georgia on July 25th before stalling and diffusing across southeastern Georgia by July 26th. Pre-frontal showers and storms moved through from northwest to southeast in the afternoon and evening of July 25th. Higher moisture and slow steering flow allowed for heavy downpours and training storms in flood-prone areas. Lower moisture and increasing subsidence aloft limited storm coverage on July 26th. Another stronger cold front moved southward across Georgia July 27th into 28th before stalling over southeast Georgia on July 29th. On July 27th, some shortwaves aloft moved through north central FL enhancing sea breeze thunderstorms. On July 29th, extreme heat, high moisture, and high mixed level CAPE ahead of the front helped develop strong to severe storms across southeast Georgia and northeast Florida.
episodes.215293: A strong ridge over the Rockies lead to hot dry surface temperatures while ushering in monsoon moisture aloft. The combination contributed to gusty showers and thunderstorms in southeast Wyoming and western Nebraska.
episodes.215852: Storms developed ahead of a cold front across northwestern Minnesota during the evening of the 24th. As these storms moved along the US 2 corridor across northern Cass and Itasca counties, hail to 2 inches in diameter was reported along with trees downed at a campground in Cass Lake.
episodes.215950: A cool front slowly shifted southward through Georgia on July 25th before stalling and diffusing across southeastern Georgia by July 26th. Pre-frontal showers and storms moved through from northwest to southeast in the afternoon and evening of July 25th. Higher moisture and slow steering flow allowed for heavy downpours and training storms in flood-prone areas. Lower moisture and increasing subsidence aloft limited storm coverage on July 26th. Another stronger cold front moved southward across Georgia July 27th into 28th before stalling over southeast Georgia on July 29th. On July 27th, some shortwaves aloft moved through north central FL enhancing sea breeze thunderstorms. On July 29th, extreme heat, high moisture, and high mixed level CAPE ahead of the front helped develop strong to severe storms across southeast Georgia and northeast Florida.
episodes.216073: Some monsoon thunderstorms produced heavy runoff in portions of Gila County.
episodes.216076: Isolated thunderstorms developed over northern Sheridan and northwestern Cherry County during the late afternoon of July 25th. These storms produced a 64 MPH wind gust east of Merriman.
episodes.216094: An active July monsoon pattern persisted throughout Utah, resulting in continued instances of flash flooding and thunderstorm winds.
episodes.216298: Severe thunderstorms tracking across northeast South Dakota produced large hail and damaging straight-line winds. Hail reached two inches in diameter near Elm Lake and Westport, topping out at 2.25 inches near Ordway. Law enforcement reported wind-driven hail with gusts estimated between 60 and 70 mph near Westport. In Barnard, strong winds snapped a large tree.
episodes.216305: Widespread thunderstorm activity generated high winds across portions of central, north central and northeast South Dakota from the late afternoon into the evening hours of July 25th. A peak wind gust of 81 mph was recorded on the South Dakota Department of Transportation (SDDOT) mesonet station near Harrold, and an 80 mph gust was recorded on the SDDOT mesonet station 4 miles west southwest of Blunt, both in Hughes County. A 79 mph gust was logged by the SDDOT mesonet station near Ree Heights (Hand County), while a 76 mph gusts was also recorded on the South Dakota State University mesonet station 5 miles north northwest of Lantry (Dewey County). An additional 32 high wind or wind related damage reports were recorded with this system. In addition to tree damage, high winds blew a semi off the highway overpass in Selby.  ||Aside from the high winds, large hail was observed as these storms developed in central South Dakota, with the public reporting 2.5 inch hail 4 miles south southwest of West Shore recreation area (Jones County), while 2 inch hail was observed west of the city of Fort Pierre.
episodes.216342: Scattered severe thunderstorms developed along a surface trough in central North Dakota, in a hot and somewhat dry air mass that led to high-based thunderstorms and predominantly a threat of damaging thunderstorm wind gusts. Supercells developed in central North Dakota during the afternoon before combining to become a line of storms that moved through the James River Valley in the evening. The most significant wind damage happened early in the event in the city of Washburn in McLean County. Trees were uprooted with enough force to lift concrete and there was extensive roof damage across the area, including at the Memorial Building, the ambulance bay, and multiple businesses. Significant corn crop damage was reported at a farm in south Washburn. Wind speeds were estimated around 100 mph. Late in the event, the largest hail report occurred, with a report of hail 3 inches in diameter near Forbes in Dickey County.
episodes.216527: A few disturbances moving through the region combined with sufficient moisture and instability allowed for a few rounds of thunderstorms between the 23rd-25th to Southwest and Central MT. The main hazard with storms was severe wind gusts.
episodes.216777: Scattered storms developed during the very late afternoon across central South Dakota, and moved into an environment of considerable instability (>4000 J/kg MLCAPE and 40-45 knots of effective deep-layer shear). Storms congealed into a broken linear structure while spreading eastward through southeast South Dakota and into southwest Minnesota and northwest Iowa by mid to late evening.  An increasing dry layer farther east allowed storms to rapidly weaken by late evening across northwest Iowa and southwest Minnesota.
episodes.216960: Some high based thunderstorms produced instances of strong downburst wind gusts across western SD on this afternoon.
episodes.217055: A supercell produced large hail across northern Grand Forks County as it tracked east during the early evening hours.
episodes.217056: Supercells developed across northwest MN during the afternoon evening hours and tracked east and southeast mainly along and north of Highway 2 merging into several small MCS clusters. These storms produced large hail to 2 inches and damaging winds.
episodes.217229: A stationary front was positioned across the Mid-South with scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. Precipitable values of more than 2 inches resulted in very heavy rainfall and isolated gusty winds. A microburst occurred over southern Tishomingo County.
episodes.217269: Thunderstorms impacted much of south-central MT, producing gusts up to 74 mph.
episodes.217281: A stalled frontal boundary near South Florida and adjacent Atlantic waters led to an unsettled weather pattern in late July.
episodes.217306: Locally heavy rainfall in Cochise county led to road closures.
